doc.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023

title: Woody Shaw, his compositions and his place in trumpet history
summary: Asked about his melodic originals, Vega talks about Woody Shaw's Sweet Love of Mine and calls Shaw the last great innovator of the trumpet, also praising Tim Hagans.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: No I’m totally onboard with that. I want to ask you about your compositions and your original music. If you — I was listening to “Sweet Love of Mine” and some things that are on your website. And I like the fact that when the song is over I can hum the melody back.
Yeah that’s a Woody Shaw composition.

See Woody’s the perfect example of that. Because Woody’s music was harmonically very intellectual. He included rhythmic elements from Brazil and as well as Afro- Caribbean rhythms and swing. And when he soloed he was applying harmonic concepts that were not really that closely related to trumpet. They’re mostly related to saxophone performance. But he played lyrically and beautiful even when he was playing his most abstract lines it was always beautiful. “Sweet Love of Mine” — beautiful composition. Woody could write beautiful melodies with very interesting chord progressions. He knew how to do it. To me Woody was one of the — Woody — I’m going to say something — Woody to me was the last great innovator of jazz trumpet in my opinion. Because he took what was there before, the schools of Louis Armstrong, Dizzy, Miles, of course he came out of a Freddie Hubbard bag. But the fact that he went into the direction applying the Coltrane things, applying the Eric Dolphy things, applying the things that he got from Larry Young, applying the things that he got from Joe Henderson. And he really changed the approach of how to play the trumpet. And I don’t think anybody’s come to — you know I could be wrong and there are so many talented — I’m not besmirching any of his contemporaries or any of the younger cats that have come out but he really did something different. I personally, I like the way Tim Hagans plays quite a bit. Because Tim comes out of that Woody thing but Tim’s also got a kind of a different thing. And he plays beautiful. Tim’s a good old friend of mine.
